To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effect of sustained compressive and/or tensile loading on the residual mechanical strength of concrete strongly depends not only on loading magnitude but also on the loading age.

compressive creep at a young age increases compressive strength, whereas compressive creep at an old age decreases compressive strength, and that tensile creep increases tensile strength at a young age.
the effect of sustained compressive load on the residual mechanical strength of concrete depends on the loading age, while the tensile creep has a negligible effect on the residual strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the residual properties of concrete subjected to a sustained loading and the results are of interest to the field of structural engineering.
the effect of creep load applied to the concrete specimens at different ages and directions.

the effect of sustained load on the residual mechanical characteristics of concrete, with the aim of providing more accurate data for the estimation of the residual load capacity and the design of concrete structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
creep leads to a decrease of the mechanical properties of concrete in the long-term.
the creep strain acts in a beneficial manner when it is induced by compressive loading at a young age and in a detrimental manner when it is caused by tensile loading at a young or old age.
compressive creep at a young age improves compressive strength while it lowers compressive strength at a later age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
compressive creep has a significant positive effect on the residual strength of concrete, while tensile creep has almost no effect.
the creep strain acts in the opposite direction for compressive and tensive loads.
creep acts to increase strength when the applied load is low and acts to reduce strength when the load is high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the residual load capacity must be evaluated for each case separately.
the creep effect should not be overlooked in the design of prestressed concrete structures.
the creep effect must be carefully considered in any study of the residual strength of a structure.
